To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

KiSS‐1 is expressed by gonadotroph cells and that its expression is positively controlled by oestradiols, while GPR54 is expressed by gonodotrophs and that its expression positively controlled by GnRH.
KiSS‐1 is up‐regulated in the female rat by oestradiols and GPR54 by GnRH.

KiSS‐1 gene is expressed in the pituitary gonadotroph and its expression is regulated by oestradiols, whereas GPR54 gene is also expressed in gonadotroph cells and its expression is up‐regulated by GnRH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the regulation of KiSS‐ 1 and GPR 54 expression, in the pituitary and the hypothalamus.
the role of kisspeptins in the control of reproduction.

the regulation of kisspeptin and GPR54 expression by gonadotrophins, oestradiol and GnRH, and the possible involvement of kisspeptins in the negative feedback exerted by oestradiols on GnRH secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kisspeptin and its receptor are expressed in gonadotroph cells, and that their expression in gonadotropes is regulated by steroids and/or GnRH.
kisspeptin is the product of the KiSS‐I gene, and its cognated receptor GPR54 is the gene product of the GPR54 gene.
KiSS‐1 is a target for oestrogen and GPR54 for GnRH in the rat pituitary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kisspeptin and its receptor are co‐expressed in gonadotroph cells and are differentially regulated by gonadotrophins and oestradiol.
, in the pituitary, the KiSS‐Kiss1R system is a target of E2 and is not directly regulated by GnRH, whereas the GnRH–GPR54 system is a target for GnRH, but is down‐regulated by E2.
the kisspeptin–GPR54 system is regulated by two different mechanisms, depending on the cell type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gonadotroph is a key site of integration of the central and peripheral actions of oestradiol and GnRH on kisspeptin and GPR54 expression.
, in the pituitary, the KiSS‐ 1 and GPR 54 genes are co‐expressed and differentially regulated by oestradiols and GnRH.

the expression of the KiSS‐ 1 and GPR 54 genes is differentially regulated in the female rat gonadotrophic cells, suggesting that the kisspeptin/GnRH axis is under the influence of both steroids and GnRH.
